Seventh-day Adventists and Baptists are Protestant Christians who affirm the authority of the Bible and practice believers’ baptism by immersion. Their main differences are in worship, church organization, and beliefs about the end times.

| Topic | Seventh-day Adventists | Baptists |
|---|---|---|
| Weekly worship | Observe the Sabbath from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset and typically worship on Saturday. | Typically worship on Sunday, with varying views on whether Sunday should be kept as a Sabbath. |
| Religious authority | Regard the Bible as the final authority and recognize Ellen G. White’s writings as a prophetic gift. | Regard the Bible as the final authority and generally give no comparable role to a modern prophet. |
| Death and the end times | Teach that the dead are unconscious until resurrection and that Christ began a distinct phase of heavenly judgment in 1844. | Generally teach that believers are consciously with Christ after death while awaiting resurrection, and hold a range of views on the end times. |
| Church organization | Belong to a worldwide denomination organized through regional conferences. | Typically govern themselves as local congregations, often choosing to join associations or conventions. |
| Health practices | Emphasize healthy living, teach abstinence from alcohol and tobacco, and encourage vegetarian diets. | Vary by congregation in their guidance on alcohol, tobacco, and diet. |

Local comparison fields — [Adventist congregation], [Baptist congregation], [location].

# mara ellis
glass artist and studio technician  
adelaide, south australia  
mara.ellis@example.com

## professional profile

adelaide-based glass artist working across kiln casting, kiln forming, and coldworking. i make freestanding sculpture and architectural panels that explore how light moves through layered colour, textured surfaces, and clear glass. my recent work draws on the changing waterlines of the port river and the light that crosses suburban interiors in the late afternoon. i manage projects from the first drawing and material tests through fabrication, installation, and documentation. alongside my studio practice, i teach introductory workshops and support artists using shared glass facilities.

## studio and employment experience

### independent glass artist | mara ellis glass, adelaide | 2021–present

- design and fabricate small sculpture editions, one-off exhibition works, and commissioned glass panels. prepare drawings, material samples, quotes, and production schedules for clients, galleries, and fabricators.
- develop a reference library of glass samples that records colour combinations, thickness, firing schedules, and surface finishes. use the samples to estimate how a proposed piece will look under the lighting available at its destination.
- produce kiln-cast sculpture using plaster-silica moulds made from clay or wax models. plan mould orientation, prepare the glass charge, and allow sufficient time for annealing and controlled cooling before releasing and finishing each piece.
- collaborate with local metalworkers and cabinetmakers on plinths, brackets, and frames. provide dimensions, estimated weights, and bearing surface details, then check that finished mounts fit before arranging delivery.
- manage studio purchasing, fabrication costs, exhibition deadlines, stock records, and packing. provide clients with handling and cleaning instructions and retain photographs and measurements for future repairs or replacements.

### glass studio technician | claybank glass workshop, bowden | 2018–2021

- prepared shared workspaces for classes and independent artists. checked kiln bookings against project dimensions and firing requirements so that artists could plan around loading, cooling, and maintenance periods.
- assisted artists with mould preparation, test firings, kiln loading, grinding, and polishing. recorded firing programs and outcomes so that repeat projects could build on earlier tests.
- maintained coldworking stations, including water feeds, grinder surfaces, splash guards, and sediment traps. tracked consumables and scheduled work around equipment servicing.
- inducted new studio members in equipment operation, handling and storage of sheet glass, and cleanup procedures. demonstrated safe lifting, wet grinding, and how to recognise when a piece needed additional support during handling.
- introduced a weekly inventory sheet for frequently used abrasives, kiln furniture, and protective equipment. made the sheet available at each workstation so tutors and members could flag low stock between scheduled checks.

### glass production assistant | harker and reed studio, thebarton | 2016–2018

- assisted with the production of fused glass lighting components and decorative panels. cut and cleaned sheet glass, prepared layouts from templates, and checked dimensions against job drawings before firing.
- finished fired pieces with wet abrasives and inspected edges, faces, and mounting points under both reflected and transmitted light. recorded defects and prepared replacement pieces when required.
- helped assemble small orders, photograph finished work, and prepare crates for interstate freight. labelled components in installation order and included drawings and packing lists for installers.

## selected exhibitions

### salt marks | quarrier project room, port adelaide | 2025

solo exhibition of seven kiln-cast sculptures based on tidal stains and painted waterline marks observed along the port river. used clear and pale green glass with alternating polished and ground surfaces. arranged the works so visitors could see how their apparent depth changed as they moved across the room.

### borrowed light | south yard gallery, norwood | 2024

group exhibition exploring light in domestic spaces. contributed three freestanding glass panels that drew on the patterns cast by verandah screens and window frames. worked with the gallery to position the panels where daylight reached them at different times of day.

### lines of drift | inland objects exhibition, mount barker | 2023

exhibited four low glass forms based on sediment patterns and fragments of shoreline debris. presented a set of test tiles alongside the finished works to show how changes in glass thickness and surface finish affected colour and translucency.

## selected commissions

### meeting room panels | alder street design office, adelaide | 2025

designed and fabricated two kiln-formed glass panels for an internal meeting room. created three full-size samples to help the client compare privacy, colour, and light transmission. coordinated frame tolerances with the joiner and mapped the location of each panel before installation.

### river stones | private commission, henley beach | 2023

produced a set of six kiln-cast objects for a recessed display shelf. developed the forms from shoreline sketches and used a combination of polished faces and satin-finished edges. supplied a placement drawing and fitted protective pads to the bases for use on the timber shelf.

## teaching and community work

- **introduction to kiln-formed glass, claybank glass workshop, 2022–present.** teach short courses for adult beginners. demonstrate glass cutting, layout, kiln preparation, and edge finishing. guide participants through a set of test tiles and a small finished piece.
- **open studio demonstrations, bowden, 2022–2025.** demonstrated mould making, wet grinding, and hand polishing during public studio events. prepared samples at different stages so visitors could handle and compare surface finishes.
- **shared studio mentoring, adelaide, 2024–present.** meet with early-career makers to review project drawings, estimate material quantities, and organise trials for new forms. help participants document their tests so they can repeat successful results when moving to larger work.

## education and professional development

- **diploma of visual arts, glass and sculpture, southern form arts college, adelaide, 2016.** final project explored how repeated cast forms changed in appearance when viewed against coloured and neutral backgrounds.
- **short course in exhibition lighting, south yard gallery, 2024.** practised positioning lights for reflective and transparent objects and compared how beam angle affected glare and shadow.
- **workshop in mould making for kiln casting, claybank glass workshop, 2019.** developed multipart moulds for irregular forms and documented dimensional changes between models and finished casts.

## technical skills

kiln casting, lost-wax mould making, sheet glass cutting, fusing, slumping, kiln programming, wet grinding, hand lapping, polishing, surface testing, technical drawing, production scheduling, exhibition installation, object photography, custom packing, stock management, and small-group instruction.

# ਸਾਫਟਵੇਅਰ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰ ਦੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਹੁਨਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਸਾਰਣੀ

| ਮਾਪਦੰਡ | ਭਾਰ | ੦ — ਅਧੂਰਾ | ੧ — ਮੁੱਢਲਾ | ੨ — ਸਮਰੱਥ | ੩ — ਉੱਨਤ |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਸਮਝਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੱਲ ਚੁਣਨਾ** | ੨੦ | ਮੁੱਖ ਲੋੜ ਗ਼ਲਤ ਸਮਝਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਾਂ ਹੱਲ ਕੰਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ। | ਮਦਦ ਨਾਲ ਆਮ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਲਈ ਹੱਲ ਲੱਭਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਲੋੜਾਂ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਆਮ ਤੇ ਸੀਮਾਵਰਤੀ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਲਈ ਢੁੱਕਵਾਂ ਹੱਲ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਸੰਭਵ ਹੱਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੇ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੇ ਆਧਾਰ ’ਤੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਚੋਣ ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਕੋਡ ਦੀ ਸਹੀਵਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਂਭ-ਸੰਭਾਲ** | ੨੦ | ਕੋਡ ਮੁੱਖ ਲੋੜ ਪੂਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ। | ਕੋਡ ਆਮ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਚੱਲਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ ਜਾਂ ਸੋਧਣਾ ਔਖਾ ਹੈ। | ਕੋਡ ਸਹੀ, ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਅਤੇ ਸੋਧਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੌਖਾ ਹੈ। | ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਕੋਡ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਨਾਲ ਮੇਲ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਲੋੜੀ ਗੁੰਝਲ ਪਾਏ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਸੰਭਾਵੀ ਸੋਧਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੌਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ** | ੧੫ | ਚੁਣੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਨਾਲ ਮੁੱਖ ਲੋੜ ਪੂਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ। | ਮੁੱਢਲੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਤਿਆਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਜ਼ਿੰਮੇਵਾਰੀਆਂ ਧੁੰਦਲੀਆਂ ਹਨ। | ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਜ਼ਿੰਮੇਵਾਰੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦਾ ਲੈਣ-ਦੇਣ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਵਧਣ ਜਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਫੇਲ੍ਹ ਹੋਣ ’ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਵਰਤੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਬਣਤਰ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਜਾਂਚ ਅਤੇ ਤਸਦੀਕ** | ੧੫ | ਮੁੱਖ ਵਿਹਾਰ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ। | ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਆਮ ਸਫਲ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਆਮ, ਸੀਮਾਵਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਅਸਫਲ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਅਜਿਹੀਆਂ ਜਾਂਚਾਂ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਵੱਡੇ ਜੋਖਮਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕਵਰ ਕਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਪੁਰਾਣੀਆਂ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀਆਂ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਣ ’ਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫੜਨ। |
| **ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਲੱਭਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰਨਾ** | ੧੫ | ਬਿਨਾਂ ਸਬੂਤ ਅਨੁਮਾਨ ਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਦੀ ਤਸਦੀਕ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ। | ਮਦਦ ਨਾਲ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਦਿਸਦੀ ਗ਼ਲਤੀ ਠੀਕ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸਬੂਤ ਨਾਲ ਕਾਰਨ ਲੱਭਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਦੀ ਤਸਦੀਕ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਸੰਭਾਵੀ ਕਾਰਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਵਾਰੀ-ਵਾਰੀ ਪਰਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਮੂਲ ਕਾਰਨ ਠੀਕ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਉਸੇ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਫੜਨ ਲਈ ਜਾਂਚ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਭਰੋਸੇਯੋਗਤਾ** | ੧੫ | ਕੰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਜਾਂ ਭਰੋਸੇਯੋਗਤਾ ਦੇ ਜੋਖਮ ਨੂੰ ਅਣਡਿੱਠਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਧਿਆਨ ਦਿਵਾਉਣ ’ਤੇ ਮੁੱਢਲਾ ਜੋਖਮ ਪਛਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਕੰਮ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਾਂ, ਮਿਲਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਅਸਫਲ ਹਾਲਾਤ ਨੂੰ ਢੁੱਕਵੇਂ ਢੰਗ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਭਾਲਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਜੋਖਮਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਅਸਰ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਤਰਜੀਹ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਤਸਦੀਕ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਉਪਾਅ ਤੇ ਅਸਫਲਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਉਭਰਨ ਦਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ। |

**ਅੰਕ ਦੇਣ ਦਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ**

- ਅਹੁਦੇ ਦੇ ਪੱਧਰ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਕੰਮ ਦੀ ਔਖਿਆਈ ਅਤੇ ਉਮੀਦਾਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਤੈਅ ਕਰੋ। ਇੱਕੋ ਅਹੁਦੇ ਲਈ ਸਾਰੇ ਉਮੀਦਵਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਲਨਾਯੋਗ ਕੰਮ, ਸਮਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦਿਓ।
- ਹਰ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਲਈ ਕੋਡ, ਜਾਂਚ ਦੇ ਨਤੀਜੇ ਜਾਂ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ ਵਰਗਾ ਠੋਸ ਸਬੂਤ ਦਰਜ ਕਰੋ। ਜੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੁਨਰ ਨੂੰ ਦਿਖਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਿਆ, ਤਾਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ **ਅਣਪਰਖਿਆ** ਦਰਜ ਕਰੋ।
- ਕੁੱਲ ਅੰਕ ਕੱਢਣ ਲਈ ਹਰ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਦੇ ਅੰਕ ਨੂੰ ੩ ਨਾਲ ਭਾਗ ਦਿਓ, ਉਸ ਦੇ ਭਾਰ ਨਾਲ ਗੁਣਾ ਕਰੋ ਅਤੇ ਨਤੀਜੇ ਜੋੜੋ। ਜੇ ਕੋਈ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਅਣਪਰਖਿਆ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਅਧੂਰਾ ਦਰਜ ਕਰੋ।

2. In your app, use Android’s `LocationManager` to request updates from `GPS_PROVIDER`, which uses satellite signals to find your position.
3. Wait for a location update. This can take a little while, especially indoors.
4. When the update arrives, call `getTime()` on the `Location` object. The result tells you when the phone got that position, measured in milliseconds since January 1, 1970 at midnight UTC.

*Early life and captivity*

Raymond III became Count of Tripoli in 1152 after his father Raymond II was murdered by members of the Assassins. He was about twelve years old. His mother Hodierna helped govern the county during his minority. Through her he belonged to the royal family of Jerusalem. In 1164 Raymond was captured at the Battle of Harim by the forces of Nur al-Din. He spent nearly a decade in captivity before securing his release. He later married Eschiva of Bures and became Prince of Galilee through their marriage. The marriage gave him a major lordship within the Kingdom of Jerusalem in addition to his own county.

*Regencies and the struggle for the crown*

Raymond served as regent for Baldwin IV after the young king came to the throne in 1174. Baldwin eventually took over the government himself. As the king’s leprosy worsened the succession became a source of conflict. Raymond later became regent for Baldwin V. The boy was the son of Baldwin IV’s sister Sibylla and died in 1186. Sibylla secured the crown and crowned her husband Guy of Lusignan as king. Raymond and his allies considered backing Isabella and her husband Humphrey of Toron. Humphrey instead pledged allegiance to Sibylla and Guy. Raymond withdrew to his lands in Galilee and made a separate truce with Saladin.

*The Battle of Hattin and Raymond’s death*

Under the terms of the truce Raymond allowed a Muslim force to pass through Galilee in May 1187. The force encountered and defeated a small contingent of Templars and Hospitallers at Cresson. Raymond then reconciled with Guy as Saladin prepared to invade the kingdom. When Saladin besieged Tiberias Raymond advised the king to keep the army near the springs at Sephoria even though his own wife was in the besieged citadel. Guy eventually ordered the army to march toward Tiberias. The troops suffered from thirst and came under sustained attack before Saladin defeated them at the Battle of Hattin in July. Raymond escaped with a small group and returned to Tripoli. He died later that year without children.
